title: Strange Footprints

beats.narrativeText: Outside the station, the learner discovers a series of unusual footprints recorded in the expedition's field notes.
Several explanations for the footprints seem possible, but only one fits all the available evidence.
The learner measures the tracks and compares them against the recorded evidence.
Careful comparison reveals similarities and differences between the possible explanations.
The learner must eliminate the unlikely explanations rather than simply guessing which one is correct.
By working through the evidence systematically, the learner justifies a single well-supported conclusion.
The learner reflects on how ruling out explanations was more useful than guessing.
This is the learner's first complete scientific investigation, and their confidence as an Explorer begins to grow.

activities.title: Measure Tracks
activities.storyContext: A series of unusual footprints has been found outside the station, recorded in the expedition's field notes.
activities.instructions: Measure the length, width and spacing of the tracks and record your measurements.
activities.output: A set of track measurements in the Explorer Journal.

activities.title: Compare Evidence
activities.storyContext: Several explanations for the tracks seem possible.
activities.instructions: Compare your measurements with the possible explanations Atlas provides.
activities.output: Notes comparing the evidence against each possible explanation.

activities.title: Identify Similarities and Differences
activities.storyContext: Only one explanation fits all of the available evidence.
activities.instructions: Identify the similarities and differences between each possible explanation and the evidence you have gathered.
activities.output: A list of similarities and differences for each explanation.

activities.title: Justify Conclusions
activities.storyContext: Explorer Academy values conclusions that eliminate unlikely explanations rather than guesses.
activities.instructions: Explain which explanation the evidence best supports, and why the others can be ruled out.
activities.output: A justified conclusion supported by evidence.

activities.title: Create a Field Guide of Track Patterns
activities.storyContext: A field guide would help future Explorers identify tracks more quickly.
activities.instructions: Sketch a simple field guide describing a few different track patterns.
activities.output: An illustrated field guide of track patterns.

activities.title: How Do Wildlife Researchers Identify Animals?
activities.storyContext: Identifying an animal from tracks alone is a real scientific skill.
activities.instructions: Find out how wildlife researchers identify animals without ever seeing them.
activities.output: None required — this is an open investigation.

prompts: Which explanation did you rule out, and what evidence helped you eliminate it?

discussionPoints: Which explanations did you rule out, and why?
How did measuring help you decide between explanations?
parentGuide.preparation: A ruler or tape measure is useful for measuring tracks.
parentGuide.assessment: Look for a conclusion that is justified by eliminating alternatives, not just a guess.

completionCriteria: Tracks measured, evidence compared, and a single well-supported conclusion justified.
